newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA BEAT NEW ZEALAND BY 52 RUNS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA BEAT NEW ZEALAND BY 52 RUNS.

text.p: World champions Sri Lanka, defending a modest total, beat New Zealand by 52 runs to enter the finals of the four-nation Independence Cup at Hyderabad on Tuesday.
Set to score 214 runs at only 4.3 runs an over, New Zealand meekly surrendered reaching 162 all out in 44.5 overs.

The Kiwis lost two early wickets. In-form opener Nathan Astle edged a sharply rising delivery off Chamanda Vaas into wicket keeper Kaluwitharana's gloves and Bryan Young mistimed a Sanjeeva De Silva delivery, edging it to the wicket keeper.
Skipper Stephen Fleming and Matthew Harne, batting steadily, built a partnership of 66 runs for the third wicket before they parted company.
Fleming, who was out lbw to a delivery from Aravinda De Silva, hit 24 includiong two boundaries. Horne followed soon, though his knock of 41 runs included two huge sixes and two boundaries.
New Zealand's slide began soon after Horne's exit as Chris Cairns and Craig McMillan fell cheaply with the total of their side reaching a paltry 120 for the loss of six wickets.
Among the Sri Lankan bowlers A.De Silva and Jayasuriya picked up two wickets each, making up for their earlier failure with the bat..
Muthiah Muralitharan and Kumara Dharmasena also picked up two wickets each.
Earlier the Sri Lankan innings also got off to a shaky start as they lost opener Sanath Jayasuriya and all rounder Aravinda De Silva to medium pacer Shane O'Conner in the early overs.

O'Connor had Jayasuriya caught at long-on by Chris Cairns in the third over when the Sri Lankan score was six and then clean bowled De Silva with a sharp beauty of a ball that penetrated his fumbling defences.
Roshan Mahanama and Romesh Kaluwitharana scored briskly with 41 and 44 respectively.
O'Connor, the left hand medium pacer who gave the Kiwis their early breaks, was the pick of the attack, taking three wickets for just 44 runs.
Kaluwitharana was adjudged man of the match as he added two stumpings behind the wickets and two catches to his contribution with the bat.

Hosts India will take on Pakistan on Wednesday in the other match in Madras. The two have a win and a loss against their names and the winner of Wednesday's match will qualify to meet Sri Lanka in the finals.
